sanskrit: sa tadā pātitas tena kapinā parvatottamaḥ buddhvā tasya kaper vegaṃ jaharṣa ca nananda ca
english: That foremost of mountains, having been dislodged by the monkey, perceived his speed, and thereupon rejoiced and was gladdened.

sanskrit: tam ākāśagataṃ vīram ākāśe samavasthitam prīto hṛṣṭamanā vākyam abravīt parvataḥ kapim mānuṣaṃ dharayan rūpam ātmanaḥ śikhare sthitaḥ
english: Pleased and with a glad heart, the mountain, assuming a human form and standing upon its own summit, addressed the hero who was moving through the sky.

sanskrit: duṣkaraṃ kṛtavān karma tvam idaṃ vānarottama nipatya mama śṛṅgeṣu viśramasva yathāsukham
english: "O best of monkeys, you have accomplished a most difficult deed. Having alighted upon my peaks, rest here at your ease."

sanskrit: rāghāvasya kule jātair udadhiḥ parivardhitaḥ sa tvāṃ rāmahite yuktaṃ pratyarcayati sāgaraḥ
english: "The ocean was nurtured by those born in the lineage of Rāghava; therefore that ocean now honours you, who are engaged in Rāma's service."

sanskrit: kṛte ca pratikartavyam eṣa dharmaḥ sanātanaḥ so 'yaṃ tat pratikārārthī tvattaḥ saṃmānam arhati
english: "To return a favour when a favour has been done — this is the eternal law. Thus the ocean, desiring to repay that debt, deserves respect from you."

sanskrit: tvannimittam anenāhaṃ bahumānāt pracoditaḥ yojanānāṃ śataṃ cāpi kapir eṣa samāplutaḥ tava sānuṣu viśrāntas tataḥ śeṣaṃ prakramatām iti
english: "Urged by deep regard on your account, the ocean has prompted me. This monkey is leaping a hundred yojanas. Let him rest upon your slopes and then proceed with the rest of the journey."

sanskrit: tiṣṭha tvaṃ hariśārdūla mayi viśramya gamyatām tad idaṃ gandhavat svādu kandamūlaphalaṃ bahu tad āsvādya hariśreṣṭha viśrānto 'nugamiṣyasi
english: "Stay, O tiger among monkeys; rest upon me and then proceed. Here are fragrant, sweet roots and fruits in abundance — taste them, O best of monkeys, and you will depart refreshed."

sanskrit: asmākam api saṃbandhaḥ kapimukhyas tvayāsti vai prakhyātas triṣu lokeṣu mahāguṇaparigrahaḥ
english: "There is indeed a bond between us as well, O chief of monkeys — a connection renowned throughout the three worlds, and attended by great virtues."

sanskrit: vegavantaḥ plavanto ye plavagā mārutātmaja teṣāṃ mukhyatamaṃ manye tvām ahaṃ kapikuñjara
english: "Among all the swift-leaping monkeys, O son of the wind, O elephant among monkeys, I regard you as the foremost."

sanskrit: atithiḥ kila pūjārhaḥ prākṛto 'pi vijānatā dharmaṃ jijñāsamānena kiṃ punar yādṛśo bhavān
english: "A guest, even an ordinary one, is worthy of honour by one who understands dharma and seeks to learn it — how much more so one such as yourself!"

sanskrit: tvaṃ hi devavariṣṭhasya mārutasya mahātmanaḥ putras tasyaiva vegena sadṛśaḥ kapikuñjara
english: "For you are the son of Māruta, the greatest of the gods, the noble one; and equal to him in speed, O elephant among monkeys."

sanskrit: pūjite tvayi dharmajña pūjāṃ prāpnoti mārutaḥ tasmāt tvaṃ pūjanīyo me śṛṇu cāpy atra kāraṇam
english: "When you, O knower of dharma, are honoured, Māruta receives honour thereby. For this reason you are worthy of my reverence — and hear also another reason for it."

sanskrit: pūrvaṃ kṛtayuge tāta parvatāḥ pakṣiṇo 'bhavan te 'pi jagmur diśaḥ sarvā garuḍānilaveginaḥ
english: "Long ago, dear one, in the Kṛtayuga, mountains had wings; they too moved in all directions with the speed of Garuḍa and the wind."

sanskrit: tatas teṣu prayāteṣu devasaṃghāḥ saharṣibhiḥ bhūtāni ca bhayaṃ jagmus teṣāṃ patanaśaṅkayā
english: "As they roamed about, the hosts of gods together with the seers, and all beings, were seized with fear lest the mountains fall upon them."

sanskrit: tataḥ kruddhaḥ sahasrākṣaḥ parvatānāṃ śatakratuḥ pakṣāṃś ciccheda vajreṇa tatra tatra sahasraśaḥ
english: "Then Sahasrākṣa, Śatakratu, enraged, cut off the wings of the mountains in thousands upon thousands of places with his thunderbolt."

sanskrit: sa mām upagataḥ kruddho vajram udyamya devarāṭ tato 'haṃ sahasā kṣiptaḥ śvasanena mahātmanā
english: "The lord of the gods approached me in fury, raising his thunderbolt; but then I was swiftly hurled away by the great-souled wind-god."

sanskrit: asmiṃl lavaṇatoye ca prakṣiptaḥ plavagottama guptapakṣaḥ samagraś ca tava pitrābhirakṣitaḥ
english: "I was cast into these salt waters, O best of monkeys, and there protected, wings concealed and body intact, by your father."

sanskrit: tato 'haṃ mānayāmi tvāṃ mānyo hi mama mārutaḥ tvayā me hy eṣa saṃbandhaḥ kapimukhya mahāguṇaḥ
english: "Thus I honour you, for Māruta is honoured by me — and through you, O chief of monkeys, I have this bond, so full of great virtue."

sanskrit: asminn evaṃgate kārye sāgarasya mamaiva ca prītiṃ prītamanā kartuṃ tvam arhasi mahākape
english: "In this matter that concerns both the ocean and myself, you, O great monkey, with a glad heart, ought to gratify us both."

sanskrit: śramaṃ mokṣaya pūjāṃ ca gṛhāṇa kapisattama prītiṃ ca bahumanyasva prīto 'smi tava darśanāt
english: "Shake off your fatigue, accept my honour, O best of monkeys, and deem our affection well-placed — I am delighted by your sight."

sanskrit: evam uktaḥ kapiśreṣṭhas taṃ nagottamam abravīt prīto 'smi kṛtam ātithyaṃ manyur eṣo 'panīyatām
english: Thus addressed, the best of monkeys replied to that foremost mountain: "I am pleased; hospitality has been rendered — let your displeasure be put aside."

sanskrit: tvarate kāryakālo me ahaś cāpy ativartate pratijñā ca mayā dattā na sthātavyam ihāntarā
english: "The time for my task presses; the day is advancing; and I have given a vow — I must not halt here in between."

sanskrit: ity uktvā pāṇinā śailam ālabhya haripuṃgavaḥ jagāmākāśam āviśya vīryavān prahasann iva
english: Having said this, the bull among monkeys, full of valour, touched the mountain with his hand and entered the sky, as if laughing as he went.

sanskrit: sa parvatasamudrābhyāṃ bahumānād avekṣitaḥ pūjitaś copapannābhir āśīrbhir anilātmajaḥ
english: The son of the wind-god was gazed upon with deep respect by both the mountain and the ocean, and was honoured with fitting benedictions.

sanskrit: athordhvaṃ dūram utpatya hitvā śailamahārṇavau pituḥ panthānam āsthāya jagāma vimale 'mbare
english: Then, soaring upward into the distance, leaving behind the mountain and the great ocean, he took to his father's path and moved through the clear sky.

sanskrit: bhūyaś cordhvagatiṃ prāpya giriṃ tam avalokayan vāyusūnur nirālambe jagāma vimale 'mbare
english: Again gaining an upward course and glancing back at that mountain, the son of Vāyu moved through the clear, unsupported sky.

sanskrit: tad dvitīyaṃ hanumato dṛṣṭvā karma suduṣkaram praśaśaṃsuḥ surāḥ sarve siddhāś ca paramarṣayaḥ
english: Seeing that second most difficult feat accomplished by Hanūmān, all the gods, the Siddhas, and the great seers extolled him.

sanskrit: devatāś cābhavan hṛṣṭās tatrasthās tasya karmaṇā kāñcanasya sunābhasya sahasrākṣaś ca vāsavaḥ
english: The divine beings gathered there were filled with joy at his act; and Sahasrākṣa Vāsava himself, along with the golden Sunābha, was pleased.

sanskrit: uvāca vacanaṃ dhīmān paritoṣāt sagadgadam sunābhaṃ parvataśreṣṭhaṃ svayam eva śacīpatiḥ
english: The wise lord of Śacī himself, Śatakratu, with his voice choked by satisfaction, spoke words to Sunābha, the best of mountains.

sanskrit: hiraṇyanābhaśailendraparituṣṭo 'smi te bhṛśam abhayaṃ te prayacchāmi tiṣṭha saumya yathāsukham
english: "O Hiraṇyanābha, O lord of mountains, I am deeply gratified with you; I grant you freedom from fear — remain here, good one, at your ease."

sanskrit: sāhyaṃ kṛtaṃ te sumahad vikrāntasya hanūmataḥ kramato yojanaśataṃ nirbhayasya bhaye sati
english: "You have rendered very great assistance to the valiant Hanūmān as he strides his hundred yojanas, offering fearlessness where danger existed."

sanskrit: rāmasyaiṣa hi dautyena yāti dāśarather hariḥ satkriyāṃ kurvatā śakyā toṣito 'smi dṛḍhaṃ tvayā
english: "This monkey goes as the emissary of Rāma, son of Daśaratha; by rendering him due honour, you have truly pleased me greatly."

sanskrit: tataḥ praharṣam alabhad vipulaṃ parvatottamaḥ devatānāṃ patiṃ dṛṣṭvā parituṣṭaṃ śatakratum
english: Then that foremost of mountains experienced immense delight, seeing the well-pleased Śatakratu, lord of the gods.

sanskrit: sa vai dattavaraḥ śailo babhūvāvasthitas tadā hanūmāṃś ca muhūrtena vyaticakrāma sāgaram
english: That mountain, thus granted the boon, remained in place; and Hanūmān in a moment had traversed the ocean.

sanskrit: tato devāḥ sagandharvāḥ siddhāś ca paramarṣayaḥ abruvan sūryasaṃkāśāṃ surasāṃ nāgamātaram
english: Then the gods, together with the Gandharvas, the Siddhas, and the great seers, addressed Surasā, the mother of the Nāgas, who was radiant as the sun.

sanskrit: ayaṃ vātātmajaḥ śrīmān plavate sāgaropari hanūmān nāma tasya tvaṃ muhūrtaṃ vighnam ācara
english: "This glorious son of the wind, named Hanūmān, is flying over the ocean; for a moment, place an obstacle before him."

sanskrit: rākṣasaṃ rūpam āsthāya sughoraṃ parvatopamam daṃṣṭrākarālaṃ piṅgākṣaṃ vaktraṃ kṛtvā nabhaḥspṛśam
english: "Assuming a most dreadful rākṣasa form, vast as a mountain, with fangs fearsome and tawny eyes, opening a mouth that touches the sky —"

sanskrit: balam icchāmahe jñātuṃ bhūyaś cāsya parākramam tvāṃ vijeṣyaty upāyena viṣadaṃ vā gamiṣyati
english: "— we wish to learn yet more of his strength and valour: whether he will overcome you by stratagems or sink into despair."

sanskrit: evam uktā tu sā devī daivatair abhisatkṛtā samudramadhye surasā bibhratī rākṣasaṃ vapuḥ
english: Thus addressed by the gods who had duly honoured her, that goddess Surasā, assuming a rākṣasa form, appeared in the middle of the ocean.

sanskrit: vikṛtaṃ ca virūpaṃ ca sarvasya ca bhayāvaham plavamānaṃ hanūmantam āvṛtyedam uvāca ha
english: Distorted, hideous, and terrifying to all, she intercepted Hanūmān as he flew and spoke these words.

sanskrit: mama bhakṣaḥ pradiṣṭas tvam īśvarair vānararṣabha ahaṃ tvāṃ bhakṣayiṣyāmi praviśedaṃ mamānanam
english: "O bull among monkeys, you have been appointed as my food by the lords; I shall devour you — enter this mouth of mine."

sanskrit: evam uktaḥ surasayā prāñjalir vānararṣabhaḥ prahṛṣṭavadanaḥ śrīmān idaṃ vacanam abravīt
english: Thus addressed by Surasā, the glorious bull among monkeys, with joyful countenance and palms joined, spoke these words.

sanskrit: rāmo dāśarathir nāma praviṣṭo daṇḍakāvanam lakṣmaṇena saha bhrātrā vaidehyā cāpi bhāryayā
english: "One named Rāma, son of Daśaratha, entered the Daṇḍaka forest together with his brother Lakṣmaṇa and his wife, the Vaideha princess."

sanskrit: asya kāryaviṣaktasya baddhavairasya rākṣasaiḥ tasya sītā hṛtā bhāryā rāvaṇena yaśasvinī
english: "Of this one, thus engaged in his duty and having earned the enmity of the rākṣasas, the glorious Sītā, his wife, has been abducted by Rāvaṇa."

sanskrit: tasyāḥ sakāśaṃ dūto 'haṃ gamiṣye rāmaśāsanāt kartum arhasi rāmasya sāhyaṃ viṣayavāsini
english: "I am going, by Rāma's command, as a messenger to her; O you who dwell in this domain, you ought to render Rāma assistance."

sanskrit: atha vā maithilīṃ dṛṣṭvā rāmaṃ cākliṣṭakāriṇam āgamiṣyāmi te vaktraṃ satyaṃ pratiśṛṇomi te
english: "Or else, having seen the Maithilī princess and Rāma of unwearied action, I shall come and enter your mouth — I solemnly promise you this."

sanskrit: evam uktā hanumatā surasā kāmarūpiṇī abravīn nātivarten māṃ kaś cid eṣa varo mama
english: Thus addressed by Hanūmān, the shape-shifting Surasā replied: "None may pass beyond me — this is my boon."

sanskrit: evam uktaḥ surasayā kruddho vānarapuṃgavaḥ abravīt kuru vai vaktraṃ yena māṃ viṣahiṣyase
english: Thus addressed by Surasā, the enraged bull among monkeys replied: "Then make your mouth large enough to take me in."

sanskrit: ity uktvā surasāṃ kruddho daśayojanam āyataḥ daśayojanavistāro babhūva hanumāṃs tadā
english: Having spoken thus to Surasā, Hanūmān in his fury became ten yojanas in length and ten yojanas in breadth.

sanskrit: taṃ dṛṣṭvā meghasaṃkāśaṃ daśayojanam āyatam cakāra surasāpy āsyaṃ viṃśadyojanam āyatam
english: Seeing him cloud-dark and ten yojanas in extent, Surasā also opened her mouth to twenty yojanas.

sanskrit: hanumāṃs tu tataḥ kruddhas triṃśadyojanam āyataḥ cakāra surasā vaktraṃ catvāriṃśat tathocchritam
english: Then Hanūmān in his fury grew to thirty yojanas; and Surasā made her mouth forty yojanas high.

sanskrit: babhūva hanumān vīraḥ pañcāśadyojanocchritaḥ cakāra surasā vaktraṃ ṣaṣṭiyojanam āyatam
english: The heroic Hanūmān became fifty yojanas in height; Surasā made her mouth sixty yojanas across.

sanskrit: tathaiva hanumān vīraḥ saptatiṃ yojanocchritaḥ cakāra surasā vaktram aśītiṃ yojanāyatam
english: Likewise the heroic Hanūmān rose to seventy yojanas; Surasā made her mouth eighty yojanas wide.

sanskrit: hanūmān acala prakhyo navatiṃ yojanocchritaḥ cakāra surasā vaktraṃ śatayojanam āyatam
english: Hanūmān, like a motionless mountain, grew to ninety yojanas; Surasā made her mouth a hundred yojanas in extent.

sanskrit: tad dṛṣṭvā vyāditaṃ tv āsyaṃ vāyuputraḥ sa buddhimān dīrghajihvaṃ surasayā sughoraṃ narakopamam
english: Seeing that gaping mouth of Surasā, terrifyingly wide and long-tongued, resembling the entrance to the netherworld, the wise son of Vāyu —

sanskrit: sa saṃkṣipyātmanaḥ kāyaṃ jīmūta iva mārutiḥ tasmin muhūrte hanumān babhūvāṅguṣṭhamātrakaḥ
english: — instantly contracted his body; like the wind within a cloud, Hanūmān at that moment became no larger than a thumb.

sanskrit: so 'bhipatyāśu tad vaktraṃ niṣpatya ca mahājavaḥ antarikṣe sthitaḥ śrīmān idaṃ vacanam abravīt
english: He swiftly darted into that mouth, then with great speed shot out of it, and standing in the sky, the glorious one spoke these words.

sanskrit: praviṣṭo 'smi hi te vaktraṃ dākṣāyaṇi namo 'stu te gamiṣye yatra vaidehī satyaṃ cāstu vacas tava
english: "O daughter of Dakṣa, I have entered your mouth — homage to you. I shall go to where the Vaideha princess is; and let your words prove true."

sanskrit: taṃ dṛṣṭvā vadanān muktaṃ candraṃ rāhumukhād iva abravīt surasā devī svena rūpeṇa vānaram
english: Seeing him freed from her mouth as the moon from the mouth of Rāhu, the goddess Surasā, in her own form, addressed the monkey.

sanskrit: arthasiddhyai hariśreṣṭha gaccha saumya yathāsukham samānaya ca vaidehīṃ rāghaveṇa mahātmanā
english: "For the success of your purpose, O best of monkeys, go, gentle one, at your ease; and reunite the Vaideha princess with the great-souled Rāghava."

sanskrit: tat tṛtīyaṃ hanumato dṛṣṭvā karma suduṣkaram sādhu sādhv iti bhūtāni praśaśaṃsus tadā harim
english: Seeing that third most difficult feat of Hanūmān, all living beings thereupon praised the monkey with cries of "Well done! Well done!"

sanskrit: sa sāgaram anādhṛṣyam abhyetya varuṇālayam jagāmākāśam āviśya vegena garuṇopamaḥ
english: He had overcome the irresistible ocean, the abode of Varuṇa, and entered the sky, moving with speed like Garuḍa.

sanskrit: sevite vāridhāribhiḥ patagaiś ca niṣevite carite kaiśikācāryair airāvataniṣevite
english: He traversed the sky frequented by cloud-bearers and birds, visited by celestial bards, and coursed by Airāvata.

sanskrit: siṃhakuñjaraśārdūlapatagoragavāhanaiḥ vimānaiḥ saṃpatadbhiś ca vimalaiḥ samalaṃkṛte
english: The sky was adorned with shining aerial cars flying about, carrying those borne by lions, elephants, tigers, birds, and serpents.

sanskrit: vajrāśanisamāghātaiḥ pāvakair upaśobhite kṛtapuṇyair mahābhāgaiḥ svargajidbhir alaṃkṛte
english: The sky was beautified by fires blazing like the crash of thunderbolts, and adorned by the meritorious and fortunate who had conquered heaven.

sanskrit: bahatā havyam atyantaṃ sevite citrabhānunā grahanakṣatracandrārkatārāgaṇavibhūṣite
english: The sky was frequented by the many-rayed fire bearing oblations without end, and was adorned with planets, constellations, the moon, the sun, and hosts of stars.

sanskrit: maharṣigaṇagandharvanāgayakṣasamākule vivikte vimale viśve viśvāvasuniṣevite
english: The sky was filled with bands of great seers, Gandharvas, Nāgas, and Yakṣas; it was clear and pure and wide, frequented by Viśvāvasu.

sanskrit: devarājagajākrānte candrasūryapathe śive vitāne jīvalokasya vitato brahmanirmite
english: He moved through the sky traversed by the elephant of the king of gods, along the path of the moon and the sun, the auspicious canopy of the world of the living, spread out and fashioned by Brahmā.

sanskrit: bahuśaḥ sevite vīrair vidyādharagaṇair varaiḥ kapinā kṛṣyamāṇāni mahābhrāṇi cakāśire
english: Frequented on all sides by heroes and by noble hosts of Vidyādharas, great clouds blazed as the monkey drew them in his wake.

sanskrit: praviśann abhrajālāni niṣpataṃś ca punaḥ punaḥ prāvṛṣīndur ivābhāti niṣpatan praviśaṃs tadā
english: Darting into masses of clouds and bursting out again and again, he shone like the moon in the rainy season, emerging and entering in turn.

sanskrit: plavamānaṃ tu taṃ dṛṣṭvā siṃhikā nāma rākṣasī manasā cintayām āsa pravṛddhā kāmarūpiṇī
english: But seeing him flying, a rākṣasī named Siṃhikā, enormous and able to assume any form at will, thought within her mind:

sanskrit: adya dīrghasya kālasya bhaviṣyāmy aham āśitā idaṃ hi me mahat sattvaṃ cirasya vaśam āgatam
english: "Today, after a long time, I shall eat my fill; this great creature has come within my power after so long."

sanskrit: iti saṃcintya manasā chāyām asya samakṣipat chāyāyāṃ saṃgṛhītāyāṃ cintayām āsa vānaraḥ
english: Having thought thus in her mind, she seized his shadow. As his shadow was seized, the monkey thought to himself:

sanskrit: samākṣipto 'smi sahasā paṅgūkṛtaparākramaḥ pratilomena vātena mahānaur iva sāgare
english: "I have been suddenly dragged back with my momentum arrested, like a great ship in the ocean struck by a contrary wind."

sanskrit: tiryag ūrdhvam adhaś caiva vīkṣamāṇas tataḥ kapiḥ dadarśa sa mahāsattvam utthitaṃ lavaṇāmbhasi
english: Looking about him to the sides, above, and below, the monkey then saw a massive creature rising from the salt sea.

sanskrit: kapirājñā yad ākhyātaṃ sattvam adbhutadarśanam chāyāgrāhi mahāvīryaṃ tad idaṃ nātra saṃśayaḥ
english: "This is the creature of marvellous appearance, the shadow-seizer of great power, about which the monkey king spoke — there is no doubt."

sanskrit: sa tāṃ buddhvārthatattvena siṃhikāṃ matimān kapiḥ vyavardhata mahākāyaḥ prāvṛṣīva balāhakaḥ
english: Having truly understood her nature, the wise monkey grew immensely large in body, like a rain-cloud of the wet season.

sanskrit: tasya sā kāyam udvīkṣya vardhamānaṃ mahākapeḥ vaktraṃ prasārayām āsa pātālāmbarasaṃnibham
english: Gazing up at the growing body of that great monkey, she stretched open her mouth to the measure of the sky and the netherworld.

sanskrit: sa dadarśa tatas tasyā vikṛtaṃ sumahan mukham kāyamātraṃ ca medhāvī marmāṇi ca mahākapiḥ
english: Then the wise great monkey saw her hideously vast mouth, and measured her body, and discerned her vital spots.

sanskrit: sa tasyā vivṛte vaktre vajrasaṃhananaḥ kapiḥ saṃkṣipya muhur ātmānaṃ niṣpapāta mahābalaḥ
english: Into her wide-open mouth the monkey, firm as a thunderbolt, abruptly contracted himself and burst out — that one of mighty strength.

sanskrit: āsye tasyā nimajjantaṃ dadṛśuḥ siddhacāraṇāḥ grasyamānaṃ yathā candraṃ pūrṇaṃ parvaṇi rāhuṇā
english: The Siddhas and Cāraṇas saw him plunging into her mouth as Rāhu swallows the full moon on a lunar day.

sanskrit: tatas tasya nakhais tīkṣṇair marmāṇy utkṛtya vānaraḥ utpapātātha vegena manaḥsaṃpātavikramaḥ
english: Then with his sharp nails the monkey tore out her vital organs, and with speed swift as thought he leapt out of her.

sanskrit: tāṃ hatāṃ vānareṇāśu patitāṃ vīkṣya siṃhikām bhūtāny ākāśacārīṇi tam ūcuḥ plavagarṣabham
english: Seeing Siṃhikā swiftly slain by the monkey and falling, the sky-ranging beings spoke to that bull among monkeys:

sanskrit: bhīmam adya kṛtaṃ karma mahat sattvaṃ tvayā hatam sādhayārtham abhipretam ariṣṭaṃ plavatāṃ vara
english: "A terrible deed has been done today; you have slain a mighty creature. Now accomplish your desired purpose — safe journey, O best of the leapers!"

sanskrit: yasya tv etāni catvāri vānarendra yathā tava dhṛtir dṛṣṭir matir dākṣyaṃ sa karmasu na sīdati
english: "He who possesses these four qualities as you do, O lord of monkeys — fortitude, foresight, intelligence, and dexterity — does not falter in his undertakings."

sanskrit: sa taiḥ saṃbhāvitaḥ pūjyaḥ pratipannaprayojanaḥ jagāmākāśam āviśya pannagāśanavat kapiḥ
english: Honoured and revered by them, his purpose well in hand, the monkey entered the sky like the devourer of serpents — Garuḍa.

sanskrit: prāptabhūyiṣṭha pāras tu sarvataḥ pratilokayan yojanānāṃ śatasyānte vanarājiṃ dadarśa saḥ
english: Having nearly reached the far shore, glancing about in all directions, he saw a line of forest at the end of the hundred yojanas.

sanskrit: dadarśa ca patann eva vividhadrumabhūṣitam dvīpaṃ śākhāmṛgaśreṣṭho malayopavanāni ca
english: And even as he flew, that best of tree-branch-dwellers saw an island adorned with varied trees, and the groves of the Malaya range.

sanskrit: sāgaraṃ sāgarānūpān sāgarānūpajān drumān sāgarasya ca patnīnāṃ mukhāny api vilokayan
english: He beheld the ocean, the ocean shores, the trees growing on those shores, and even the faces of the ocean's consorts.

sanskrit: sa mahāmeghasaṃkāśaṃ samīkṣyātmānam ātmanā nirundhantam ivākāśaṃ cakāra matimān matim
english: The wise one, reflecting upon himself — vast as a great cloud, as if blocking the sky — resolved within his mind:

sanskrit: kāyavṛddhiṃ pravegaṃ ca mama dṛṣṭvaiva rākṣasāḥ mayi kautūhalaṃ kuryur iti mene mahākapiḥ
english: "The rākṣasas, upon seeing my great size and speed, will take an undue interest in me" — so the great monkey reasoned.

sanskrit: tataḥ śarīraṃ saṃkṣipya tan mahīdharasaṃnibham punaḥ prakṛtim āpede vītamoha ivātmavān
english: Thereupon he contracted that mountain-like body and returned to his natural form, like one free of delusion — composed and self-possessed.

sanskrit: sa cārunānāvidharūpadhārī paraṃ samāsādya samudratīram parair aśakyapratipannarūpaḥ samīkṣitātmā samavekṣitārthaḥ
english: He who could assume many beautiful forms, having reached the far shore of the ocean, wore a form that none of his enemies could anticipate — he had reflected upon himself and surveyed his purpose.

sanskrit: tataḥ sa lambasya gireḥ samṛddhe vicitrakūṭe nipapāta kūṭe saketakoddālakanālikere mahādrikūṭapratimo mahātmā
english: Then that great soul, rivalling the peak of a mighty mountain, alighted upon the richly adorned, variegated summit of Mount Lamba, with its ketakī, uddālaka, and nālikera trees.

sanskrit: sa sāgaraṃ dānavapannagāyutaṃ balena vikramya mahormimālinam nipatya tīre ca mahodadhes tadā dadarśa laṅkām amarāvatīm iva
english: Having by his power traversed that ocean filled with Dānavas and Nāgas, garlanded with great waves, and having alighted upon the shore of the great sea, he then beheld Laṅkā, like Amarāvatī.
